name: Privacy
description: A single-file H5 stock privacy screen. A permission is not a checkbox, it is an edge in a graph: every app declares named features and which permissions each one needs, so revoking something does not print a warning — it names the features that stop working. Some permissions depend on others: precise location is meaningless without location and is dropped with it, and «Always» location quietly degrades to «While using» the moment background refresh goes off. The headline number is not a score but a query — how many apps can find out where you are while you are not looking. Three can, and getting that to nought without losing turn-by-turn navigation or the outdoor run route means knowing which feature actually needed «Always». 5 screens, 8 apps, 9 permissions, 19 named features.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

world.graph: 8 apps, 9 permissions, 19 features; each feature names the permissions it needs and the level it needs them at
world.implications: precise location requires location; «Always» requires background refresh and silently degrades to «While using» without it
world.seeded: Compass Maps, Cirrus Weather and Stride Fitness all have Always + background refresh; Chatter, Marketplace and Streamly are allowed to track; nothing is broken
world.headline: the number on top is a query over the matrix — apps with location = Always and background refresh on — not a score
world.costs: stopping all background location breaks exactly 3 features and keeps navigation, lane guidance and the run route; revoking location everywhere breaks 8, two of them only because precise location goes with it; revoking tracking everywhere breaks 2 and costs Chatter nothing
